title: Address an envelope
description: Address an envelope so a postal worker can find the recipient and the return address.
oneStarDescription: Write a recipient and an address in the order your postal service shows on its example.
twoStarDescription: Add a return address where it will not be confused with the destination.
threeStarDescription: Read it as if you did not know the person, and correct one ambiguity.

title: Agree a simple exchange
description: Agree a small trade or split where both people can point to what they give and get.
oneStarDescription: Say what you offer and what you want, and ask the other person to say theirs.
twoStarDescription: Change one term, such as time or amount, and restate the whole agreement.
threeStarDescription: Write the agreement in two sentences both people accept, including what happens if one person cannot do it.

title: Annotate a text
description: Mark a text with questions and definitions so you can reread only your marks.
oneStarDescription: Mark one sentence you do not understand and write the question beside it.
twoStarDescription: Look up one hard word and write a short meaning you will understand later.
threeStarDescription: Read only your marks and say what the text is about, then check one point against the page.

title: Arrange a small display
description: Arrange a few objects so a viewer can tell which one is the focus.
oneStarDescription: Place one object as the focus and say why the eye should go there.
twoStarDescription: Add two other objects that do not steal the focus, and ask a viewer where they looked first.
threeStarDescription: Move or remove the object that stole attention, and show the difference.

title: Ask a question that gets an answer
description: Ask a question that the other person can answer from what they know.
oneStarDescription: Ask one question that does not contain two questions, and wait for the answer.
twoStarDescription: Ask a follow-up that uses a word the person actually said.
threeStarDescription: If the person cannot answer, rewrite the question or stop, and say which you did.

title: Ask for directions and repeat them
description: Ask for directions and repeat them back so the person can correct you.
oneStarDescription: Ask for the way to a specific place, and let the person finish.
twoStarDescription: Repeat the steps in order and ask if you have them right.
threeStarDescription: Write one landmark they gave you, and what you will do if you do not see it.

title: Ask for help specifically
description: Ask for a specific kind of help, from a person who can give it, by a time.
oneStarDescription: Write what you need, in a form another person could do.
twoStarDescription: Ask someone who can actually help, and include a time.
threeStarDescription: Record whether they agreed, refused, or offered a smaller help, and thank them.

title: Blot a fresh stain
description: Blot a fresh wet stain with water and stop before you add a chemical.
oneStarDescription: Blot a fresh wet stain with a clean cloth and water, lifting rather than scrubbing.
twoStarDescription: Look at the cloth and say whether the stain is lighter, and stop if it is spreading.
threeStarDescription: If a mark remains, say you will read a care label or ask before using any cleaner, and do not invent one.

title: Braid a cord
description: Braid three strands into a cord that stays together at the ends.
oneStarDescription: Fasten three strands and braid until the pattern repeats.
twoStarDescription: Show a length where the strands are equally tight, and redo a loose bit.
threeStarDescription: Stop the end so it does not unravel, and hang a light object from the cord.

title: Braid hair so it holds
description: Braid hair, with permission, so the braid stays for ordinary movement.
oneStarDescription: Divide the hair into three sections that start evenly.
twoStarDescription: Braid to the end and fasten it so it does not immediately fall apart.
threeStarDescription: Ask whether it pulls, and loosen a start that the person says is too tight.

title: Brew coffee you can adjust
description: Brew a cup of coffee and change one variable so you can say how the taste moved.
oneStarDescription: Brew one drink and say whether it tastes too bitter, too weak, or about right.
twoStarDescription: Brew again, changing only the amount of coffee or the contact time, and say what changed in the taste.
threeStarDescription: Brew a cup for someone else, ask what they notice, and name one change you would still try.

title: Build a checklist from a miss
description: After something goes wrong, write a checklist that would have caught it.
oneStarDescription: Write what went wrong in one sentence.
twoStarDescription: Write the check that would have shown the problem before it happened.
threeStarDescription: Use the checklist on the next similar task and tick the new item.

title: Cancel an unwanted subscription
description: Find a subscription you did not mean to keep and cancel it through the service's own path.
oneStarDescription: Point to a repeating charge on a statement and the name of the service.
twoStarDescription: Open the cancellation path on the service you already use, not a link from an unexpected message.
threeStarDescription: Save the confirmation or the end date, and say what you will check on the next statement.

title: Change a plan when transport fails
description: When a ride is cancelled or missed, choose the next way and tell a person who is waiting.
oneStarDescription: Write what failed and the time you noticed.
twoStarDescription: Choose the next available way from information you can show, and the new arrival time.
threeStarDescription: Tell the person who is meeting you the new time, and what you will do if that ride fails too.

title: Check a home before you leave
description: Walk a short checklist before you leave home, and fix one thing the list catches.
oneStarDescription: Write the checks that matter for your home, such as the cooker, the taps, the windows, and the lock.
twoStarDescription: Walk the list and tick only what you looked at.
threeStarDescription: Find one item that was not ready, fix it or decide to stay, and say which.

title: Check a receipt
description: Check a receipt against what you bought and the prices you were shown.
oneStarDescription: Match each line on a receipt to an item you bought, and mark a line you cannot match.
twoStarDescription: Add the lines or use the printed sum and the tax, and say whether the total matches.
threeStarDescription: If something is wrong, say what you would ask the seller to change, or say the receipt matches.

title: Check an automated answer
description: Ask a software tool a question and check the answer against a source you can open.
oneStarDescription: Ask for a fact you can check, and save the answer.
twoStarDescription: Open a source you trust and mark one part of the answer that matches and one that you cannot find.
threeStarDescription: Rewrite only the part you could source, and leave out the rest.

title: Choose a gift for a person
description: Choose a gift from what you know about a person, and say what you are not assuming.
oneStarDescription: Write one interest or need you have actually seen or been told.
twoStarDescription: Choose a gift that matches that fact, within a budget you wrote down.
threeStarDescription: Name one assumption you will not use, such as age or gender, and show the gift does not depend on it.

title: Choose with written reasons
description: Make a choice you can explain from reasons you wrote before you decided.
oneStarDescription: Write the decision and two real options.
twoStarDescription: Write one reason for and one reason against each option, using facts you can point to.
threeStarDescription: Choose one option, then write the strongest reason you did not follow.

title: Cite a source in a note
description: Attach a citation a reader could follow to a claim in your note.
oneStarDescription: Write a claim and the source you took it from, including the title.
twoStarDescription: Add the author, the date, and a page or a link the reader could use.
threeStarDescription: Mark which sentence is the source's and which is your summary.

title: Clap a written rhythm
description: Clap a simple written rhythm and keep the beat under it.
oneStarDescription: Clap a short written pattern of long and short notes while you can see it.
twoStarDescription: Tap the pulse with a foot while the hands clap the pattern.
threeStarDescription: When you stumble, stop, count that bar, and clap it correctly once.

title: Clear a drain with a plunger
description: Use a plunger on a slow drain and stop if the water does not move.
oneStarDescription: Seat a plunger over the drain and show that the cup covers the hole.
twoStarDescription: Plunge until the water flows, or stop after a short try and say that it did not.
threeStarDescription: Name one sign that ends this method, such as water rising elsewhere or a drain you do not know.

title: Compare two accounts of one event
description: Read two accounts of the same event and list what they both say and where they differ.
oneStarDescription: Read two short accounts and write one sentence each says.
twoStarDescription: Write one point they share and one point they do not.
threeStarDescription: Name which difference you cannot settle from these two texts alone.

title: Compare two routes
description: Compare two ways to get somewhere by time, changes, and cost.
oneStarDescription: Write two routes with their main steps.
twoStarDescription: Compare time, number of changes, and cost or effort, using figures you can point to.
threeStarDescription: Choose one and name the fact that would make you switch.

title: Compare unit prices
description: Compare two products by the price per unit, not by the package size alone.
oneStarDescription: On two packages, point to the price and the amount.
twoStarDescription: Work out the price for the same unit on both, and show the arithmetic.
threeStarDescription: Choose one and name a reason other than unit price, such as an ingredient you need to avoid.

title: Compost kitchen scraps
description: Add kitchen scraps to a compost setup and keep out what does not belong.
oneStarDescription: Put an allowed fruit or vegetable scrap into a compost bin or pile you are allowed to use.
twoStarDescription: Name one kitchen waste you will not add, and why this setup refuses it.
threeStarDescription: Look at the pile, say whether it is too wet or too dry to the eye, and add dry material or pause scraps accordingly.

title: Convert a unit and check
description: Convert a measure from one unit to another and check the result a second way.
oneStarDescription: Convert a length, a mass, or a temperature with a factor you can show.
twoStarDescription: Check the result by reversing the conversion or by a second source, and show that it agrees.
threeStarDescription: Use the converted number in a real choice, such as whether an object fits, and say what would change the choice.

title: Cook dried beans until tender
description: Turn dried beans into tender beans and notice when they are still hard in the middle.
oneStarDescription: Soak or boil dried beans by a method printed on the packet or a recipe you can show, then taste one bean.
twoStarDescription: Cut or bite a bean from the middle of the pot and say whether the center is still chalky.
threeStarDescription: Season the finished beans, keep them hot or cool them, and say how you would tell they should not be eaten later.

title: Cook onions until sweet
description: Cook onions slowly until they soften and sweeten, and stop before they burn.
oneStarDescription: Cook sliced onions until they turn translucent and taste milder than raw.
twoStarDescription: Keep cooking until the onions are golden and taste sweet, and show that they are not black.
threeStarDescription: Add the onions to a simple dish and say what they changed compared with using them raw.

title: Cook pasta and sauce it
description: Cook pasta to the doneness you want and combine it with a sauce so the pasta is coated.
oneStarDescription: Boil pasta, taste a piece, and say whether you want it softer before you drain it.
twoStarDescription: Combine the drained pasta with a sauce so a piece is coated rather than sitting in a puddle.
threeStarDescription: If the dish is dry or watery, change it with pasta water or a thicker spoon of sauce, and show the result.

title: Cook vegetables to a chosen texture
description: Cook a vegetable so it is tender, crisp, or browned, and show the difference.
oneStarDescription: Cook one vegetable until it matches a texture you named before you started.
twoStarDescription: Cook the same vegetable two ways and point to the difference a diner would feel.
threeStarDescription: If a piece is underdone or mushy, say what you would do with it next, and do that if it can still be eaten.

title: Crop a photo without changing the event
description: Crop a photo to strengthen the subject without removing a fact that changes the story.
oneStarDescription: Crop a photo so the subject is easier to see, and keep a copy of the original.
twoStarDescription: Say what left the frame and whether the event is still the same.
threeStarDescription: Show a crop you will not use because it hides a person or an object that matters, and say why.

title: Decline a request clearly
description: Say no to a request so the other person knows the answer and what, if anything, you can do.
oneStarDescription: Decline a real or practice request in one sentence that contains the word no or an equivalent.
twoStarDescription: Add one true reason without a long apology, and stop.
threeStarDescription: If you can do a smaller part, offer that part, or say there is no alternative you can take.

title: Descale a kettle as the label says
description: Remove scale from a kettle using only the steps printed on a descaling product.
oneStarDescription: Read the product label aloud for the amount and the wait, and show the kettle unplugged or empty of a brew.
twoStarDescription: Carry out the printed steps and rinse as the label says.
threeStarDescription: Point to one thing you did not do because it was not on the label.

title: Divide work in a small group
description: Split a task so each person knows their part and how the parts meet.
oneStarDescription: Write the parts of a small task and who takes each one.
twoStarDescription: For one part, write what finished looks like and when it is needed.
threeStarDescription: Put the parts together and name one gap between them.

title: Document a process
description: Document a process with ordered steps and a picture or sketch of the tricky part.
oneStarDescription: Write the steps of a process you just did, in the order you did them.
twoStarDescription: Add a photo or sketch of the step that is hard to say in words.
threeStarDescription: Follow the document from the start, or have someone else do so, and fix one wrong order.

title: Draw a rough floor plan
description: Draw the outline of a room and the doors, good enough to plan where a table goes.
oneStarDescription: Draw the walls and mark the door.
twoStarDescription: Add the large furniture in places that match the room, and check by looking.
threeStarDescription: Draw one piece in a new place and say whether the door still opens.

title: Draw an object you are looking at
description: Draw an object in front of you, and correct one proportion from a second look.
oneStarDescription: Draw the outer shape of an object while you look at it.
twoStarDescription: Compare one width or height with the object and change the drawing.
threeStarDescription: Add one shadow or overlap you missed, and point to it on the object.

title: Empty a dryer lint filter
description: Clean a dryer lint filter before a cycle and say why the lint should not stay there.
oneStarDescription: Remove the lint filter and show the lint that was on it.
twoStarDescription: Seat the filter the way the machine expects and start only if it sits flat.
threeStarDescription: Point to a panel you are not opening, and say the filter skill stops at the screen you can lift out.

title: Estimate how long work takes
description: Guess how long a task will take, do it, and compare the guess with what happened.
oneStarDescription: Before you start a familiar task, write how long you think it will take.
twoStarDescription: After the task, write the time it took and the difference from the guess.
threeStarDescription: Estimate a second task and say which part of the first result changed your number.
